title: Left ventricular geometry as a risk factor for recurrent subaortic stenosis after primary resection.
authors: Alaa Aman Felimban; Heba Abdel-Ghafar Hessuin Mohamed; Muna Ismail; Ibrahim J Alibrahim; Husam I Ardah; Fahad Alhabshan; Mohamed Salim Kabbani
abstract:
Discrete subaortic stenosis is a progressive cause of left ventricular outflow tract obstruction in children, and recurrence after surgical resection is not uncommon. We evaluated echocardiographic and morphologic factors associated with reintervention after primary subaortic membrane resection.
We conducted a single-centre retrospective cohort study of paediatric patients (0-14 years) who underwent primary surgical resection of subaortic membrane stenosis between 2002 and 2019. Demographic, clinical, and echocardiographic variables were compared between patients requiring reintervention and those requiring a single operation. Independent predictors were assessed using multivariable logistic regression.
Seventy-seven patients were included; 16 required reintervention and 61 did not. On univariate analysis, the reintervention group had higher preoperative left ventricular outflow tract peak and mean gradients and shorter membrane length. In multivariable analysis, shorter membrane length independently predicted reintervention (adjusted odds ratio 0.677 per 1-mm increase, 95% confidence interval 0.487-0.941; p = 0.020), as did higher preoperative left ventricular outflow tract peak gradient (adjusted odds ratio 1.066 per 1-mmHg increase, 95% confidence interval 1.023-1.111; p = 0.002). A smaller aorto-septal angle showed a trend towards increased risk but did not reach statistical significance (adjusted odds ratio 0.933, 95% confidence interval 0.866-1.005; p = 0.067). Aortic regurgitation was significantly worse at follow-up in patients requiring reintervention.
Shorter subaortic membrane length and higher preoperative left ventricular outflow tract peak gradient were independent predictors of reintervention after primary resection. These findings may improve risk stratification and support closer echocardiographic surveillance of patients at increased risk of recurrence.

title: Does thrombocytopenia predict short-term mortality after transcatheter and surgical aortic valve replacement?
authors: Volkan Burak Taban; Abdullah Güner; Yakup Alsancak; Yüksel Dereli; Niyazi Görmüş
abstract:
Postprocedural thrombocytopenia is frequently observed after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) and surgical aortic valve replacement (sAVR), but its independent prognostic value remains unclear. We investigated whether platelet reduction after TAVI and sAVR independently predicts short-term mortality beyond baseline procedural risk.
This retrospective single-center study included 216 patients who underwent aortic valve replacement between 2015 and 2020. Sixty-seven patients underwent TAVI and 149 underwent sAVR. Mechanical valve recipients were retained in the overall cohort but excluded from the primary TAVI-sAVR comparison. Propensity score overlap weighting was used to reduce baseline differences between groups. Longitudinal changes in platelet count (PLT), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), and platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR) were evaluated using generalized estimating equation models, and factors associated with 90-day mortality were assessed using Firth penalized logistic regression.
The primary comparative cohort included 67 TAVI and 93 sAVR patients. After overlap weighting, adequate balance was achieved for all measured baseline covariates. Significant treatment × time interactions were observed for PLT (p = 0.001), NLR (p < 0.001), and PLR (p = 0.002). On postprocedural day 3, moderate thrombocytopenia was more frequent after sAVR than TAVI (33.5% vs. 8.3%), whereas normal platelet levels were more frequent after TAVI (45.6% vs. 8.2%; overall p < 0.001). Weighted 90-day mortality did not differ significantly between TAVI and sAVR (12.6% vs. 17.5%, p = 0.487). In Firth regression models, only EuroSCORE II remained independently associated with 90-day mortality.
Postprocedural platelet and inflammatory responses showed different temporal patterns after TAVI and sAVR. However, these biomarker changes were not independently associated with 90-day mortality after adjustment, whereas EuroSCORE II remained independently associated with mortality. Serial hematological changes should therefore be interpreted together with baseline clinical risk rather than as isolated prognostic markers.

title: Single-center clinical analysis of anomalous aortic origin of a coronary artery (AAOCA) in children: a multimodal imaging approach to risk stratification.
authors: Tao Wang; Haijie Qi; Yanli Xie; Xiaoyuan Feng; Li Gong
abstract:
This study aimed to analyze the clinical characteristics of pediatric patients with Anomalous Aortic Origin of a Coronary Artery (AAOCA), explore the application of multimodal imaging in risk stratification, and establish individualized diagnosis and treatment protocols for this population.
A retrospective observational study was performed on children diagnosed with AAOCA at Wuhan Children's Hospital between January 2015 and April 2026. Clinical manifestations, multimodal imaging findings, therapeutic strategies, and long-term outcomes were comprehensively analyzed.
A total of 58 AAOCA patients confirmed by coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) were enrolled. Initial transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) yielded false-negative results in 24 patients (41.4%). Twenty-seven patients underwent single-photon emission computed tomography myocardial perfusion imaging (SPECT-MPI, MPS), among whom 6 had normal perfusion and 21 showed perfusion defects. Seven patients with positive MPS findings received surgical correction, including 2 patients with L-AAOCA( 1 coronary angioplasty and 1 coronary unroofing) and 5 patients with R-AAOCA; all treated with coronary unroofing. No patients with negative MPS results underwent surgery, indicating that negative MPS findings perhaps provide limited valuable evidence to avoid unnecessary coronary revascularization. Two patients developed massive postoperative pericardial effusion and recovered after pericardiotomy and drainage; the remaining 5 surgical patients experienced no perioperative complications. All surgical patients were discharged after full recovery and received 3 months of aspirin antiplatelet therapy. Non-surgical patients were instructed to restrict strenuous physical activity and followed up for 3 months to 3 years. Follow-up CCTA or TTE revealed normal coronary ostia without stenosis in all patients.
Clinical manifestations of pediatric AAOCA vary widely across age groups, ranging from asymptomatic presentation to sudden cardiac arrest (SCA), leading to marked discrepancies in risk evaluation and therapeutic decision-making. Multimodal imaging including TTE, CCTA and SPECT-MPI facilitates risk stratification and guides personalized clinical management of children with AAOCA.

title: Deep Learning and Dual-Domain Fusion of Temporal and Spectrotemporal SCG for Valvular Heart Disease Classification.
authors: Junseob Kim; Tilendra Choudhary; Md Hassanuzzaman; Rishikesan Kamaleswaran
abstract: Heart valve disease (HVD) is a growing cause of cardiovascular morbidity, yet accessible screening tools remain limited. Tri-axial seismocardiogram (SCG) signals capture mechanical signatures of both stenosis and regurgitation, but their non-stationary nature and subtle inter-lesion morphological differences challenge robust classification from a single representation. This study proposes an electrocardiogram (ECG)-free dual-domain deep learning framework that combines a 1D convolutional-recurrent encoder of raw SCG waveforms with a 2D EfficientNet encoder of continuous wavelet transform scalograms, integrating temporal and spectrotemporal representations through feature-level fusion. The framework was evaluated on primary valve lesion classification in 94 patients, with an additional exploratory analysis of multi-valvular, aortic-stenosis-dominant disease. Under patient-level stratified group cross-validation, the fused model achieved the highest mean accuracy (65.3%; 95% CI, 59.8-70.7%), exceeding both unimodal encoders and the majority-class (35.2%) and covariate-only (39.1%) baselines. The same mean performance ordering was preserved when the image backbone was replaced, although the confidence intervals overlap at this cohort size. Under the segment-level protocol used in prior studies, the framework achieved 99.63% accuracy, with faster training convergence and more compact, separable feature clusters than either unimodal encoder. These findings support the value of combining temporal and spectrotemporal SCG representations and demonstrate its potential for ECG-free HVD classification under patient-independent evaluation.

title: Effects of SGLT2 inhibition on cardiac remodeling and heart failure development in aortic stenosis rats.
authors: Luana U Pagan; Mariana J Gomes; Mariana Gatto; Gustavo A F Mota; João Pedro G Oliveira; Felipe C Damatto; Lidiane M Souza; Eder A Rodrigues; Anna Clara C Santos; Gabriela H Tukiyama; Dijon H S Campos; Marcel Rodrigues Ferreira; Camila R Correa; Gilson M Murata; Bertha F Polegato; Marina P Okoshi; Katashi Okoshi
abstract: Aortic stenosis (AS) is increasingly prevalent in ageing populations, yet no pharmacological therapy has been shown to modify its progression to heart failure (HF). Sodium glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors improve outcomes in HF, but their effects in pressure overload-induced cardiac remodeling remain unclear. Here, we show that rats with long-term AS develop HF features, left ventricular dilation, and systolic and diastolic dysfunction, accompanied by increased oxidative stress, impaired antioxidant defenses, myocardial fibrosis, and transcriptional remodeling. Empagliflozin (10 mg/kg/day for 8 weeks) attenuated cardiac dysfunction and reduced HF features. At molecular level, empagliflozin prevented increase in lipid peroxidation, and decreased interstitial collagen deposition, while increasing glutathione peroxidase and matrix metalloproteinase-2 activity. Transcriptomic analysis identified 1,078 differentially expressed genes and revealed enrichment of pathways associated with extracellular matrix organization and signal transduction in AS. Empagliflozin predominantly regulated genes involved in cardiac contraction, mitochondrial membrane organization, apoptosis, and cell survival. Profibrotic and remodeling-associated genes were upregulated in AS, while empagliflozin induced a distinct transcriptional program associated with improved myocardial homeostasis. AS was associated with reduced activity of energy metabolism enzymes, which was not restored by empagliflozin. Collectively, these findings identify oxidative stress, extracellular matrix remodeling, and transcriptional reprogramming as mechanisms underlying cardiac dysfunction in AS. Empagliflozin mitigates cardiac remodeling and HF progression and modulates fibrosis and gene networks regulating cardiac function. These data highlight SGLT2 inhibition as a potential therapeutic strategy in pressure overload-induced heart failure.

title: Aortic valve replacement and concomitant coronary artery bypass grafting: technical considerations in the era of sutureless and rapid-deployment aortic valves.
authors: Dimos Karangelis; Theodora M Stougiannou
abstract:
Coexistence of severe aortic stenosis (AS) and coronary artery disease (CAD) is frequently encountered in contemporary practice, particularly amongst elderly patients with multiple comorbidities. Although transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) combined with percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) has emerged as an alternative strategy, surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) with concomitant coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) remains the reference treatment for these patient groups. The introduction of sutureless and rapid-deployment aortic valves (RDAV) has considerably expanded the surgical armamentarium, by facilitating implantation, and reducing cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) and aortic cross-clamp times. Appropriate application of these technologies requires specific technical considerations that ultimately influence operative planning and execution.
This review summarizes contemporary evidence associated with the use of sutureless and RDAVs in combined CABG and SAVR procedures. To ensure relevant literature is included, a literature search across PubMed and ScienceDirect has been carried out, spanning the last 20 years, utilizing relevant medical subject headings (MeSH) terms and keywords.
As evidence on sutureless and RDAVs technologies continues to accumulate, with associated advancements in perioperative planning, these valves are expected to become valuable adjuncts in combined procedures, by minimizing operative burden while also allowing for robust, aortic valve pathology correction.

title: Impaired NK Cell-Mediated Tumor Surveillance in Atherosclerosis Due to Plaque-Induced PPARα Dysfunction.
authors: Tong Ren; Shengnan Yu; Xilin Jiang; Jing Wen; Changsheng Yan; Dan Du; Jian Tang; Lu Peng; Sangang Wu; Cuilian Dai; Enhui Yao; Xin Jin; Lichao Yang
abstract:
Atherosclerosis is frequently associated with both an increased incidence and accelerated development of cancer. However, the impact of atherosclerosis progression on the efficacy of tumor surveillance by cytotoxic immune cells, particularly natural killer (NK) cells, remains poorly understood. This study aims to explore how atherosclerosis affects NK cell-mediated tumor surveillance in both animal models and humans.
We analyzed peripheral blood NK cells from patients with atherosclerosis with early-stage (<50% stenosis) versus advanced-stage (≥50% stenosis) coronary artery lesions by flow cytometry to assess NK cell frequency, PPARα (peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha) expression, and IFN-γ (interferon gamma) production. In parallel, we used atherosclerotic plaque progression and regression models, including high-fat diet-fed Apo-/- mice and aortic arch transplantation into wild-type, Apoe-/-, Rag1-/-, and NK cell-specific PPARα knockout (Pparaflox/flox Ncr1Cre/+) mice. NK cell phenotype and function were evaluated by flow cytometry for immune checkpoint molecules (PD-1 [programmed cell death protein-1], TIM-3 [T-cell immunoglobulin and mucin-domain containing-3], LAG-3 [lymphocyte activation gene-3], and TIGIT [T-cell immunoglobulin and ITIM domain]) and effector cytokines (IFN-γ, GZMB [granzyme B]). Antitumor capacity was assessed in B16F10 melanoma and ID8 ovarian cancer models in atherosclerosis mice, with or without a PPARα agonist (oleoylethanolamide) or an mTOR (mechanistic target of rapamycin kinase) agonist (MHY1485) treatment. Mechanistic studies included immunoblotting for mTOR pathway components and transcriptomic correlation analyses (GSE94044, GSE24495).
We found that atherosclerotic plaques induced PPARα deficiency in NK cells, which impaired their cytotoxicity and weakened tumor immunosurveillance. Mechanistically, PPARα-deficient NK cells exhibited elevated immune checkpoint expression, an exhaustion phenotype, and markedly diminished mTOR signaling. Administration of the PPARα agonist oleoylethanolamide restored NK cell effector function and enhanced tumor-killing efficacy in vivo, whereas mTOR agonism partially rescued the defect caused by PPARα loss. These findings underscore the suppressive effects of arterial plaques on NK cell-mediated antitumor immunity and suggest PPARα compensation as a potential immunotherapeutic strategy.
Our study unveils a novel association between atherosclerosis and the attenuation of NK cell antitumor immunity. Specifically, plaque-induced downregulation of PPARα in NK cells leads to uncontrolled immune checkpoint expression, causing NK cell exhaustion and diminished antitumor function. Pharmacological enhancement of PPARα signaling rejuvenated NK cell activity and reduced tumor growth in atherosclerosis. Therefore, targeting PPARα offers a promising therapeutic approach for cancer treatment and prevention in individuals with atherosclerosis.

title: Prevalence and prognostic impact of valvular heart disease in transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis.
authors: Camille Sarrazyn; Philippe Debonnaire; Mathias Claeys; Francesca Graziani; Maria Chiara Meucci; Erwan Donal; Madelien Regeer; Fausto Jose Pinto; Steven Droogmans; Nico Van de Veire; Philippe Bertrand; Ching Hui Sia; Arnold Ng; Ruxandra Jurcut; Robert Adam; Kensuke Hirasawa; Takeru Nabeta; Caroline Van De Heyning; Nicole Sturkenboom; Jeroen J Bax; Nina Ajmone Marsan
journal: Amyloid : the international journal of experimental and clinical investigation : the official journal of the International Society of Amyloidosis
abstract:
Significant valvular heart disease (VHD) is associated with adverse prognosis in transthyretin amyloidosis cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM). However, data is limited to isolated VHD. We aimed at evaluating the difference in outcome between isolated and multiple VHD, and particularly with and without aortic stenosis (AS).
Patients with ATTR-CM were retrospectively included in a multicentric registry. The endpoint was a composite of heart failure hospitalizations and all-cause death.
Of the 694 patients (mean age 75 ± 13 years,74%male), 302(44%) presented with significant VHD. Of these, 98 had VHD including AS (isolated AS in 45%;multiple VHD with AS in 55%), while 204 had VHD without AS (isolated in 64%, multiple VHD in 36%). During a median follow-up of 22(8-38) months, 217(31%) patients reached the endpoint. Significant VHD was associated with worse outcomes than no-VHD (log-rank p < 0.001; HR:3.275; 95%CI (2.472-4.337), remaining significant after adjustment (HR2.006 (1.193-3.047);p = 0.007). Stratification by the presence of AS, and according to isolated or multiple VHD, revealed that isolated significant AS ((HR: 2.462; 95%CI (1.233-4.917); p = 0.011), and multiple VHD including significant AS, had the highest risk for adverse outcomes ((HR: 3.385; 95%CI (1.744-6.573);p < 0.001).
In ATTR-CM, significant VHD is strongly associated with poor prognosis, with the highest risk for adverse events in significant multiple VHD including AS.

title: Perioperative Management of a Spinal Cord Stimulator During Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation: A Case Report.
authors: Jonathan Zheng; Julian Yeoh; Matias Yudi; Anoop N Koshy; Laurence Weinberg
abstract: Spinal cord stimulation (SCS) is an established treatment for chronic neuropathic pain, and patients with an implanted stimulator are presenting with increasing frequency for transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). We describe an 88-year-old man with a high-frequency (10 kHz) spinal cord stimulator for chronic back pain who underwent transfemoral TAVI under sedation for severe symptomatic aortic stenosis. After consultation with the implanting pain service, the stimulator was switched off with the patient's own remote control, which was kept in the procedure room; rapid ventricular pacing was delivered through a bipolar right ventricular lead so that the pacing current was confined to the myocardium and remote from the pulse generator; and external defibrillator pads were positioned away from the generator and the course of the leads. The procedure was uneventful. The patient tolerated the interruption of therapy without clinically significant pain; a new left bundle branch block after valve deployment was identified on an artefact-free trace, stimulation was resumed after the procedure with analgesia equivalent to baseline, and subsequent interrogation confirmed normal device function. The case illustrates the application of a precautionary strategy informed by manufacturer labelling and analogous evidence; because the stimulator was off throughout, it does not establish that any individual measure was necessary. We examine how the hazards of the cardiac catheterisation laboratory differ from those of the operating theatre and propose a structured six-step approach to the management of a spinal cord stimulator during TAVI.

title: Developing proficiency in a transcatheter aortic valve replacement program: lessons from a single academic center's learning curve.
authors: Emiliano Gabriel Manueli Laos; Andres Fontaine-Nicola; Lily Zhang; Andrew Carlson; Mario A Masrur; Amer K Ardati; Khalil Ibrahim; Adhir Shroff; Khaled Abdelhady
journal: Indian journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery
abstract:
Aortic stenosis (AS) is a prevalent and high-mortality valve disease. Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is a minimally invasive treatment with outcomes often better than surgery, requiring a multidisciplinary team. This study analyzes outcomes and trends from a high-volume TAVR program in an urban, low-income setting since 2017 to guide future practices.
Medical records of patients that underwent TAVR were analyzed retrospectively from 2018 to 2023, dividing them into two cohorts to analyze trends in operative details, complications, length of stay (LOS), and readmission/mortality rates. The learning curve (LC) was assessed by operative time.
Risk-adjusted cumulative sum (RA-CUSUM) analysis identified the transition point at case 76, dividing the cohort into early LC phase group (n = 76) and post-LC phase group (n = 190). Median operative time decreased from 106 to 80 minutes. After adjustment, operative time was 14% shorter in the post-learning-curve cohort (GMR 0.86, 95% CI 0.77-0.96; p = 0.005).
Operative time serves as a useful benchmark for institutional maturation. In our program, reaching 76 cases represented a key transition point toward optimized workflows, enhanced efficiency, and improved resource utilization.

title: [Acquired von Willebrand syndrome associated with mechanical circulatory support].
authors: Kenki Saito
journal: [Rinsho ketsueki] The Japanese journal of clinical hematology
abstract: Acquired von Willebrand syndrome (AVWS) is an acquired hemostatic abnormality characterized by quantitative or qualitative defects of von Willebrand factor (VWF). In high-shear conditions, such as aortic stenosis (AS) or mechanical circulatory support (MCS), excessive proteolytic cleavage of von Willebrand factor (VWF) by its specific protease ADAMTS13 leads to the loss of large-molecular-weight VWF multimers. AVWS is increasingly recognized as a potential risk factor for bleeding in patients on MCS. Current management strategies for AVWS associated with MCS include VWF supplementation with fresh frozen plasma or VWF concentrate; however, the therapeutic effect is only transient due to persistent VWF degradation. Our research group developed a humanized anti-ADAMTS13 antibody (HA10), and we are currently developing a novel therapeutic strategy to control bleeding symptoms associated with AVWS by inhibiting ADAMTS13 activity. We demonstrated the efficacy of HA10 in inhibiting VWF degradation in MCS-implanted male cynomolgus monkeys and further established its safety profile in a GLP-grade single-dose intravenous toxicity study in male cynomolgus monkeys. Our data indicate a potentially low risk of thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura, a potentially severe complication associated with HA10.

title: Rationale for Early Discontinuation of Aspirin After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation: Design of the SOLOTAVI Randomized Trial.
authors: Farzin Beygui; Christophe Caussin; Stéphanie Marlière; Guillaume Bonnet; Eric Durand; Thibaud Lhermusier; Jean-Francois Morelle; Stéphane Delépine; Géraud Souteyrand; Said Ghostine; Eric Van Belle; Olivier Barthélémy; Mariama Akodad; Guillaume Cayla; Chekrallah Chamandi; Frank Chemouni; Jean-Jacques Parienti; Claire Bouleti; Hélène Eltchaninoff; SOLOTAVI Investigators
abstract:
Trans-aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has become the first line treatment of aortic stenosis, a condition predominantly affecting elderly patients. In absence of a specific indication for antithrombotic therapy, lifetime aspirin is recommended after TAVI while it may be discontinued 3 months after bioprosthetic surgical valve replacement. Primary prevention, using aspirin compared to placebo among elderly patients is associated with an increased risk of major bleeding and no reduction rates of thrombotic events. Hence, there is a gap of knowledge on whether aspirin should be continued >3 months after TAVI.
SOLOTAVI is a multicenter, open label, blinded endpoint assessment, 1:1 randomized, non-inferiority trial comparing aspirin discontinuation 3 months after TAVI (experimental) to long-term therapy (control). Adult patients with successful transfemoral TAVI for symptomatic aortic stenosis and no indication or contraindication for long-term antithrombotic therapy will be enrolled. Randomization is stratified on center and valve type. The primary endpoint is the 12-month composite of all cause death, myocardial infarction, stroke, and non-procedure-related major or disabling bleeding. A hierarchical analysis is performed for the primary and 3 principal secondary endpoints. The sample size is computed for demonstrating the non-inferiority of the experimental strategy compared with the control strategy, with a conservative non-inferiority margin of 6.5%. A total of 1400 patients will be enrolled.
The SOLOTAVI trial will assess the non-inferiority of a 3-month duration of aspirin compared to the long-term therapy after successful transfemoral TAVI in terms of thrombotic and bleeding events. NCT06518317 clinicaltrials.org.

title: Carotid Endarterectomy Versus Trans-Carotid Artery Revascularisation (TCAR) for Asymptomatic Carotid Stenosis A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Karina Domingos Rosa Schneidwind; Reza Mofidi
abstract:
The treatment for asymptomatic carotid artery stenosis includes a surgical or interventional approach in selected cases. Although endarterectomy should be considered over stenting for selected patients, according to the latest European Society of Vascular Surgery (ESVS) guidelines, the Carotid Revascularization and Medical Management for Asymptomatic Carotid Stenosis Trials (CREST-2) suggested that carotid stenting would be associated with low rates of perioperative stroke or death. The transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR) technique is a relatively new endovascular method, which involves placing a stent at the carotid bifurcation through direct carotid artery access, performed under a flow reversal system. This approach avoids manipulation of the aortic arch, potentially reducing embolic events. The aim of this systematic review is to compare TCAR with carotid endarterectomy (CEA) in asymptomatic patients undergoing carotid intervention. It seeks to evaluate whether TCAR is associated with improved perioperative outcomes, such as lower rates of stroke and death, compared with CEA, given its potentially less invasive approach.
The review was performed according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) on the platforms PubMed/Medline, OVID/Embase, and Scopus. The following MeSH terms were used: "asymptomatic carotid stenosis" AND "carotid endarterectomy", "transcarotid artery revascularization" OR "TCAR". Full-text screening and data extraction were performed with the support of the COVIDENCE platform. Six studies were selected for this systematic review, comprising a total of 132,684 patients (30,581 undergoing TCAR and 102,103 undergoing CEA). Statistical analysis was performed using R software.
The selected studies for this systematic review showed similar results in terms of perioperative stroke and death for asymptomatic patients who underwent carotid endarterectomy and TCAR.
Our results suggest that there are no significant differences between CEA and TCAR for the treatment of asymptomatic patients who require a surgical or interventional approach. Further studies are necessary to provide more robust data in this field.

title: Echocardiographic atrial and right heart to pulmonary circulation coupling indices identify high-risk in moderate aortic stenosis.
authors: Gloria Santangelo; Andrea Faggiano; Giulio Pio Federico Mallardi; Michele Baroni; Luca Donisi; Alessandro Guareschi; Guido Pasero; Fabiola Sozzi; Massimiliano Ruscica; Marco Guazzi; Stefano Carugo; Francesca Bursi
abstract:
Emerging evidence points on an increased mortality risk associated to moderate aortic stenosis (AS), yet this population remains insufficiently characterized. We tested the prognostic value of two echocardiographic coupling indices reflecting right and left-sided cardiac function: the ratio of tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion to pulmonary artery systolic pressure ratio (TAPSE/PASP) and the left atrial volumetric/mechanical coupling index (LACI).
Retrospective, single-center study including 135 patients with moderate AS. TAPSE/PASP was used as a non-invasive surrogate of right ventricular-pulmonary circulation (RV-Pc) coupling, and LACI was defined as ratio of left atrial volume index to mitral a' velocity. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality. Cox regression and Kaplan-Meier analyses were used to assess the prognostic value of both indices.
During a mean follow-up of 1.61 ± 0.79 years, 33 patients (24%) died. Reduced TAPSE/PASP (< 0.67 mm/mmHg) and elevated LACI (> 5.17) were independently associated with an increased mortality (HR: 3.03 and 3.16, respectively, p < 0.01). These associations remained significant even after adjusting for age. Stratification into three groups - preserved, single, or combined uncoupling -showed progressively lower 1-year survival rates, ranging from 95% to 49% (p < 0.0001). None of the coupling-derived variables was associated with hemodynamic progression or need of aortic valve replacement.
TAPSE/PASP and LACI are independently associated with mortality in patients with moderate AS. These parameters may provide incremental prognostic information in this often-overlooked population. These findings may prompt further studies evaluating the potential role of these parameters in helping to refine prognostic phenotyping.

title: Tricuspid aortic valve morphology predicts favorable midterm outcomes after aortic valve neocuspidization in children.
authors: Guanxi Wang; Sen Zhang; Kai Ma; Kunjing Pang; Benqing Zhang; Keming Yang; Shoujun Li
abstract:
To evaluate the midterm outcomes of the aortic valve neocuspidalization (AVNeo) procedure for aortic valve reconstruction in 83 pediatric patients with complex aortic valve disease and to identify risk factors associated with the outcomes.
A retrospective analysis was conducted on pediatric patients who underwent the AVNeo procedure between January 2017 and June 2025. The composite primary end point included all-cause mortality, reoperation, or moderate-to-severe aortic valve dysfunction (regurgitation or stenosis). Univariate and multivariate Cox proportional hazards models were used to identify risk factors.
Among the 83 patients (mean age 7.0 ± 3.7 years; 67.5% male) included in the analysis, the predominant preoperative pathology was moderate-to-severe aortic regurgitation (88.0%). Single-leaflet reconstruction (65.1%) using autologous pericardium (94.0%) was the most common surgical approach. Over a mean follow-up of 28.4 ± 23.9 months, 27 patients (32.5%) met the composite end point, including 2 late deaths, 18 cases of moderate-to-severe regurgitation, and 9 cases of moderate-to-severe stenosis; 10 patients underwent reoperation. The probability of freedom from the primary end point was 83.6%, 64.5%, and 54.4% at 1, 3, and 6 years, respectively. Multivariable analysis identified tricuspid aortic valve morphology as an independent protective factor against the primary end point (hazard ratio, 0.408; 95% CI, 0.178-0.935, P = .034), whereas the use of autologous pericardium showed a strong protective trend (hazard ratio, 0.284; 95% CI, 0.078-1.037, P = .057).
AVNeo provides midterm outcomes that support its use as an alternative strategy. Tricuspid aortic valve morphology is a strong predictor of favorable outcomes, and the use of autologous pericardium demonstrates significant potential as a protective factor.

title: Long-term outcomes of transcatheter versus surgical aortic valve replacement in patients aged 70 years and older: An overlap-weighted analysis.
authors: Rieko Kutsuzawa; Naonori Kawamoto; Kimito Minami; Satoshi Kainuma; Kizuku Yamashita; Kota Suzuki; Takashi Kakuta; Ayumi Ikuta; Yuki Tadokoro; Yojiro Machii; Kentaro Mitsui; Shinichi Kurashima; Yuki Irie; Atsushi Okada; Kensuke Takagi; Makoto Amaki; Hideaki Kanzaki; Yasuhide Asaumi; Takeshi Kitai; Chisato Izumi; Satsuki Fukushima
abstract:
To compare long-term outcomes of transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) and surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) in patients aged 70 to 89 years with aortic stenosis (AS).
In this single-center retrospective study, 1100 patients who underwent primary TAVR (n = 599) or SAVR (n = 501) between 2008 and 2023 were included. An overlap-weighted propensity-score analysis was conducted using 36 baseline variables, including age, procedural year, frailty scale, Society of Thoracic Surgeons risk score, New York Heart Association class, history of coronary artery and cerebrovascular disease, and AS severity. The primary end point was the composite of all-cause mortality or cerebrovascular events.
During long-term follow-up, the composite end point occurred more frequently after TAVR than after SAVR. In the overlap-weighted analysis, TAVR was associated with a greater risk of the composite outcome (hazard ratio [HR], 1.8; 95% CI, 1.1-3.0; P = .024), with Kaplan-Meier curves diverging early and remaining separated. All-cause mortality did not differ between the groups (HR, 1.2; 95% CI, 0.7-2.1; P = .426); however, cerebrovascular events occurred predominantly after TAVR and remained significantly more frequent after overlap weighting (HR, 15; 95% CI, 2.8-89; P = .002).
In the overlap-weighted population of patients aged 70 to 89 years with AS, SAVR and TAVR were associated with comparable all-cause mortality; however, cerebrovascular events occurred more frequently after TAVR.

authors: Naoki Iwasa; Mamu Shimizu; Tomoko Okamoto; Hiroto Kosuga; Nayu Morikita; Mifumi Kawabe; Munetaka Iwata; Kazuhiro Watanabe; Yui Kobatake; Satoshi Takashima; Naohito Nishii
abstract:
Circulating fibroblast growth factor-23 (FGF-23) is primarily a kidney-related biomarker, but also may be influenced by cardiovascular remodeling and hemodynamic load.
Verify whether serum FGF-23 concentration increases with myxomatous mitral valve disease (MMVD) severity.
Forty-two client-owned dogs with MMVD without overt kidney disease.
Retrospective cross-sectional study to evaluate serum FGF-23, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), atrial natriuretic peptide (ANP), blood urea nitrogen (BUN), creatinine (Cr), and symmetric dimethylarginine (SDMA) concentrations. Imaging variables included vertebral heart score (VHS), vertebral left atrial size (VLAS), left atrial-to-aortic root ratio (LA/Ao), normalized left-ventricular internal diameter in diastole (LVIDDN), and diastolic transmitral E-wave velocity (E-vel). Differences among American College of Veterinary Internal Medicine stages were analyzed using the Kruskal-Wallis test with Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise comparisons. Correlations were analyzed using Spearman's correlation. Multivariable linear regression analysis was performed to identify factors associated with serum FGF-23 concentration.
Dogs with ACVIM stages C and D had higher serum FGF-23 concentrations than those with stages B1 and B2 (P < .05). Serum FGF-23 concentrations were positively correlated with VLAS (rs = 0.500, P < .01), ANP (rs = 0.455, P < .01), LA/Ao (rs = 0.384, P < .05), E-vel (rs = 0.372, P < .05), and NT-proBNP (rs = 0.366, P < .05). ACVIM stage was significantly associated with serum FGF-23 concentration after adjustment for serum Cr concentration and loop diuretic use.
The potential influence of MMVD should be considered when interpreting increased circulating FGF-23 concentrations in dogs with MMVD.

title: Severe Hypercoagulability With Nonbacterial Thrombotic Endocarditis After KRAS Inhibitor Exposure: A Perfect Storm.
authors: Cecilia Villa-Etchegoyen; Raymond B Fohtung; Kwan S Lee; Chadi Ayoub; Reza Arsanjani
abstract:
Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis (NBTE) is a rare malignancy-associated condition causing systemic embolization and valvular dysfunction. Its presentation as new severe mitral regurgitation (MR) may be difficult to recognize.
A 76-year-old man with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma developed progressive dyspnea after treatment with the KRAS inhibitor daraxonrasib. Echocardiography demonstrated new severe MR with leaflet thickening and broad-based echodensities. His course was complicated by pulmonary embolism, recurrent coronary thrombosis, and persistently negative blood cultures. Transesophageal echocardiography confirmed bilateral leaflet involvement with a central coaptation defect. Anticoagulation was changed to low-molecular-weight heparin.
NBTE should be considered in patients with malignancy presenting with new MR and thrombotic events without evidence of infection. The temporal association with KRAS inhibition is noteworthy but does not establish causality.
NBTE may present as subacute MR. Echocardiography and clinical context are essential for timely diagnosis and management.

title: Can the QTc interval and T-wave morphology change intermittently in arrhythmogenic mitral valve prolapse? First paediatric case experience.
authors: Senem Özgür; Serpil Kaya Çelebi; Selman Kesici; Murat Akkus; Yakup Ergul
abstract:
Mitral valve prolapse is typically considered a benign condition. However, a newly described repolarisation anomaly known as arrhythmogenic mitral valve prolapse syndrome is closely associated with repolarisation disturbances and can potentially lead to sudden cardiac death. Arrhythmogenic mitral valve prolapse syndrome is characterised by bileaflet mitral valve prolapse, mitral valve regurgitation, T-wave inversions in the inferolateral leads, and complex ventricular ectopy.
In this case, we present the diagnosis of arrhythmogenic mitral valve prolapse syndrome in a 16-year-old adolescent girl who experienced sudden cardiac arrest during exercise. Her electrocardiograms revealed intermittent QT/QTc prolongation. Interestingly, QT prolongation was always associated with T wave inversion in inferolateral leads. Heterozygous genomic changes were detected in the KCNH2 gene and the 25th exon of the ANK2 gene. These findings support the diagnosis of arrhythmogenic mitral valve prolapse syndrome in this patient.
Since mitral valve prolapse is a common condition in the society, it is important to determine beforehand which ones are at risk of sudden death. As these boundaries are drawn better, underdiagnosis as well as overdiagnosis will be prevented.

title: Decompensated heart failure after one year of successful therapy with mavacamten: a case report.
authors: Giulia Marchionni; Lucrezia Netti; Silvia Stavagna; Cristina Chimenti
abstract:
Cardiac myosin inhibition is the first disease-specific therapeutic strategy for obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Mavacamten, the first-in-class agent, has demonstrated an excellent safety profile and sustained efficacy in both clinical trials and real-world practice. However, its safe use requires careful monitoring and thorough patient education regarding potential drug-drug interactions.
We report a case of acute heart failure occurring after long-term clinical stability on mavacamten following concomitant fluconazole administration. It is reasonable to assume that the pharmacokinetic interaction resulted in excessive mavacamten exposure, leading to transient systolic dysfunction, severe functional mitral regurgitation, and adverse left ventricular remodelling.
This case report highlights the consequences of pharmacological interactions between mavacamten and a strong CYP2C19 inhibitor. Drug-drug interaction should always be considered and systematically excluded in a patient presenting with unexplained heart failure and left ventricular remodelling during mavacamten therapy.

title: Snare-Assisted Retrieval of a Mechanically Locked-Open TEER Device: A Novel Bailout Technique.
authors: Dhamodaran Kaliyamoorthy; Kannan Murugesan; Aishwarya Mahesh Kumar; Krishnaswamy Chandrasekaran
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
abstract: Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) is an established intervention for patients having severe mitral regurgitation (MR) with prohibitive surgical risk. Complications during deployment related to device malfunction are uncommon but necessitate prompt decision-making and management. A 54-year-old gentleman with dilated cardiomyopathy, severe left ventricular dysfunction, and severe MR underwent TEER using the MyClip system (Meril Life Sciences Pvt. Ltd., Vapi, Gujarat, India). Initial deployment across the A2-P2 scallops of mitral leaflets achieved partial MR reduction. Significant residual MR required a second clip for optimal leaflet coaptation. While deploying the second clip, it failed to close because of a mechanical locking failure. So, we everted the clip, pulled back to LA, and it stayed in open position and failed to close. We report a novel bailout snare technique that enabled safe retrieval without the need for a second transseptal puncture. The ability to close the clip arms prior to withdrawal minimized the risk of tearing the atrial septum and facilitated the successful completion of the TEER procedure. Another clip was deployed successfully, resulting in significant MR reduction. This case demonstrates a rare complication during deployment, a malfunction of the device, and a novel strategy for safely bailing out a challenging intra-procedural complication.

title: A Leak before the Beat: Diastolic Atrioventricular Regurgitation in Conduction Disease.
authors: Thomas Holman; Mikhail Torosoff
abstract: • Diastolic MR and TR are common findings in AVB. • Diastolic MR and TR reflect delayed valve closure, not primary valve disease. • Diastolic regurgitant jets are typically central and low velocity. • Diastolic MR and TR can signal elevated end-diastolic ventricular pressure.

title: Prospective multicenter study of murmur localization and stage-associated murmur grading in dogs with echocardiographically diagnosed cardiac diseases: the LISTEN study.
authors: Gerhard Wess; Jens Häggström; Julia Stadler; Lara König; Katarzyna Kraszewska; Doris Bittenecker; Oriol Domenech; German Santamarina; Gregory Van den Noortgate; Mikkel Brandt Bjerknaes; Jenny Eberhard; Karin Kriström; Liva Vatne; Michał Gajewski; Christel Schinner-Peters; Guy Tater; Marin Torti; Christoph Schummer; Ingrid Ljungvall
abstract:
Cardiac auscultation remains fundamental in dogs with suspected cardiac disease, but large prospective datasets describing clinician-recorded murmur localization and intensity across echocardiographic diagnoses are limited. This study aimed to characterize point of maximal intensity (PMI) patterns in dogs with echocardiographically diagnosed cardiac abnormalities and to evaluate the association between murmur grade and disease stage in dogs with myxomatous mitral valve disease (MMVD) and dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM).
This prospective international multicenter observational study included 6,996 client-owned dogs examined by 50 cardiology-trained veterinarians. Dogs underwent standardized cardiac auscultation at four predefined thoracic locations and transthoracic echocardiography during the same clinical visit. PMI localization was described across cardiac diagnoses, and murmur grade was evaluated in relation to disease stage in MMVD and DCM.
Dogs with MMVD and DCM predominantly had a left apical PMI, whereas congenital outflow tract diseases and patent ductus arteriosus were predominantly associated with a left basilar PMI. Tricuspid regurgitation and ventricular septal defect were more commonly associated with right apical and right basilar PMIs, respectively. In MMVD, murmur intensity increased with advancing disease stage (p < 0.001), and dogs with a murmur greater than soft had higher odds of being in stage B2 or C/D than B1 (OR 35.9, 95% CI 27.6-46.6). In DCM, 25.8% of dogs had no audible murmur. Although murmur grade distribution differed across DCM stages (p = 0.03), intensity did not show a consistent stage-associated increase.
Clinician-recorded four-point auscultation identified characteristic regional PMI patterns across several canine cardiac diseases. Murmur grade was strongly associated with disease stage in MMVD but provided limited stage-related information in DCM. Auscultation may support initial clinical assessment and prioritization of differential diagnoses, but echocardiography remains essential for definitive diagnosis and staging.

title: Impact of left ventricular reshaping on postinfarction functional mitral regurgitation in a chronic swine model of advanced heart failure.
authors: Kosuke Nakamae; Chihiro Miyagi; Junya Matsuda; Syed Faizullah Hussaini; Tatsuya Watanabe; Satoshi Yuhara; Adrienne Morrison; Kirsten Nelson; Filip Konecny; Daisuke Onohara
abstract:
The study objective was to evaluate the efficacy and feasibility of left ventricular reshaping in a swine model of late-stage ischemic heart failure with marked left ventricular dilation and functional mitral regurgitation.
A chronic heart failure model with ischemic mitral regurgitation was established in 8 Yorkshire swine via percutaneous injection of 100% ethanol into the left circumflex artery. The left ventricular reshaping device was implanted transapically at 6 months postinfarction and evaluated with echocardiography and pressure-volume loop analysis. The final efficacy analysis included 7 animals.
The device was successfully implanted and significantly reduced mitral regurgitation (regurgitant volume: 43.29 ± 14.47 mL vs 9.90 ± 5.12 mL, P = .0026). Posterior excursion angle (22.71 ± 6.92° vs 39.14 ± 7.29°, P = .0042) and coaptation length (2.72 ± 0.44 mm vs 4.42 ± 0.76 mm, P = .0033) increased significantly. Left ventricular volume significantly decreased after reshaping (indexed end-diastolic volume: 140.30 ± 28.28 mL/m2 vs 84.68 ± 18.51 mL/m2, P = .0019; indexed end-systolic volume: 91.54 ± 24.01 mL/m2 vs 48.23 ± 16.25 mL/m2, P = .0003). Ejection fraction significantly increased (33.71% ± 3.30% vs 43.43% ± 7.12%, P = .0046), whereas load-independent indices of systolic function and measures of diastolic function did not change significantly.
Transapical left ventricular reshaping demonstrated acute efficacy and feasibility at 6 months postinfarction in advanced heart failure by reducing left ventricular volume and mitral regurgitation.

title: Influence of concomitant mitral valve intervention on late survival in patients with moderate ischemic mitral regurgitation undergoing surgical revascularization.
authors: Sameer K Singh; Arnar Geirsson; Ernest Traad; Paul Kurlansky; George Ebra
abstract:
In patients with moderate ischemic mitral regurgitation, the influence of concomitant mitral valve (MV) intervention at the time of revascularization on late survival remains unclear. The purpose of this study was to compare the lifetime survival of patients with moderate ischemic mitral regurgitation who underwent revascularization alone versus concomitant MV repair or replacement.
Retrospective review was performed for 776 consecutive patients, ages 65 years and older with coronary artery disease and moderate ischemic mitral regurgitation who underwent isolated coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) (n = 372), CABG with MV repair (n = 131, CABG + MV repair), or CABG with MV replacement (n = 273, CABG + MV replacement) from 1976 to 2005. Propensity score matching, Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, and Cox regression were used to compare perioperative and long-term survival. Cross-sectional follow-up utilized the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention National Death Index as well as government and genealogical internet sites, publicly available online obituaries, and death notices. Follow up was 98% complete.
The mean age of the cohort was 74.1 ± 5.8 years with 42.4% female patients. Preoperatively, 54.5% had prior myocardial infarction, 47.7% had a history of congestive heart failure, and 69.1% had an abnormal ejection fraction. Matched patients undergoing CABG or CABG + MV repair had similar incidence of major perioperative morbidity (29.0% vs 22.1%; P = .202) and operative mortality (8.4% vs 6.1%; P = .475). Late survival was similar between groups (P = .630). Among matched patients undergoing CABG versus CABG + MV replacement, those undergoing concomitant replacement had significantly increased perioperative major morbidity (35.2% vs 20.9%; P < .001) and operative mortality (16.9% vs 7.7%; P < .001). CABG + MV replacement patients experienced an increased risk of late mortality (hazard ratio, 1.23; 95% CI, 1.01-1.49; P = .035), compared with those undergoing isolated CABG.
In patients with moderate ischemic mitral regurgitation undergoing surgical revascularization, concomitant MV repair did not demonstrate a clear late survival benefit over isolated CABG, whereas concomitant MV replacement was associated with increased early and late mortality risk.

title: Mitral repair for moderate ischemic mitral regurgitation in patients with end-stage ischemic cardiomyopathy.
authors: Yusuke Misumi; Daisuke Yoshioka; Shin Yajima; Takuji Kawamura; Ai Kawamura; Kazuma Handa; Akinobu Ohtani; Shunsuke Saito; Kazuo Shimamura; Shigeru Miyagawa
abstract:
For patients with end-stage ischemic cardiomyopathy undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), the indications for concomitant repair of moderate mitral regurgitation (MR) remain controversial. This study evaluated outcomes of concomitant mitral valve repair (MVr) for moderate ischemic MR in patients with advanced left ventricular (LV) remodeling and severely impaired LV function undergoing CABG.
We retrospectively reviewed 341 patients (mean age, 67 ± 9 years) with ischemic cardiomyopathy (LV ejection fraction, ≤40%) and less-than-severe MR who underwent CABG. Of these, 108 (32%) underwent concomitant MVr for clinically relevant moderate MR, and 233 (68%) underwent CABG alone for mild or absent MR. All patients had a prior myocardial infarction. The primary end point was overall survival. Secondary end points included postoperative changes in MR grade and LV function at 1 year. Median follow-up was 4.5 years (interquartile range, 2.4-7.3 years).
Despite higher preoperative surgical risk in the CABG + MVr group (European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation II score, 6.7% vs 2.9%; P < .001), 30-day mortality did not differ between groups (1.9% vs 2.1%; P = .88). Five-year overall survival was 73% versus 77% (log-rank P = .25). At 1 year, the CABG + MVr group demonstrated greater LV reverse remodeling (median LV end-diastolic volume index reduction: -26% vs -19%; P = .001), higher LV ejection fraction (46 ± 13% vs 42 ± 12%; P = .044), and a lower prevalence of significant MR (6% vs 13%; P = .032).
In patients with advanced ischemic cardiomyopathy and moderate MR, concomitant MVr can be performed with acceptable operative risk and promotes superior LV reverse remodeling. Long-term survival was comparable to patients with nonsignificant MR who did not require mitral intervention, suggesting that targeted mitral repair may normalize the adverse prognostic influence of moderate ischemic MR.

title: Left ventricular ejection fraction decline shortly after mitral valve operation and associated survival.
authors: Kavya Rajesh; Megan Chung; Luis Gisli Rabelo; James Lao; Julia Kim; Marco Tagliafierro; Berk Inan; Ian Mason; Nathan Ott; Vivian Zhang; William Mitchell; Isaac George; Makoto Mori; Arnar Geirsson
abstract:
Reduction in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is common after mitral valve (MV) repair or replacement in patients with mitral regurgitation (MR). This study aims to evaluate the trajectory of postoperative LVEF reduction after MV surgery and determine whether this change in LVEF is associated with clinical outcomes.
This is a retrospective study of 625 patients who underwent MV surgery for moderate/severe MR between 2015 and 2023. Patients with aortic valve pathology, concomitant aortic procedures, endocarditis, and previous MV operations were excluded. Patients were divided into 4 quartiles on the basis of pre- and postoperative percent difference in LVEF. In-hospital outcomes and long-term mortality using Kaplan-Meier analysis were compared between groups. Cubic spline adjusted for preoperative LVEF was used to determine the impact of percent LVEF difference on mortality. Spaghetti plots depicted the trajectory in LVEF over a 2-year follow-up period.
Patients were divided into percent LVEF reduction quartiles as follows: severely reduced (159 [25.4%], greater than -19%), moderately reduced (157 [25.1%], between -19% and -8%), stable (171 [27.4%], between -7% and +4%), and increased (138 [22.1%], greater than a +4%). Baseline characteristics were similar. There was no difference in the percent of patients undergoing MV repair versus replacement across LVEF reduction groups (P = .55). Postoperative outcomes were similar between groups, including reoperation for bleeding, stroke, and atrial fibrillation. Long-term survival probability over 7 years was similar between all 4 groups (P = .35). There was no significant change in hazards ratio for long-term mortality across range of LVEF differences. Patients with severely or moderately reduced LVEF postoperatively remained with a depressed LVEF during the 2-year follow-up period, whereas patients with the same or increased postoperative LVEF returned to baseline.
Reduction in LVEF is common after MV repair or replacement with effects persisting after 2 years. Changes in LVEF after MV operation do not appear to affect clinical outcomes and may by itself not accurately reflect myocardial dysfunction related to MR and subsequent intervention.

title: Five-year outcomes of chordal replacement therapy for primary mitral regurgitation: The CHAGALL (CHordArt System Study for the Treatment of Mitral ReGurgitAtion due to Leaflet ProLapse or fLail) study.
authors: Alberto Weber; Kestutis Rucinskas; Jodi Akin; Maurizio Taramasso; Michel Zuber; Rolf Vogel; Andrej Podkopajev; Vilius Janusauskas; Diana Zakarkaite; Thomas Bauer; Thierry Carrel
abstract:
The CHAGALL (CHordArt System Study for the Treatment of Mitral ReGurgitAtion due to Leaflet ProLapse or fLail) study is a prospective, first-in-human early feasibility study evaluating the technical feasibility, the long-term safety, and device durability of a novel chordal replacement system for the treatment of primary degenerative mitral regurgitation.
Five patients with symptomatic severe primary degenerative mitral regurgitation attributable to isolated central posterior leaflet prolapse or flail underwent surgical implantation of the ChordArt chordal replacement system through a left atrial approach under cardiopulmonary bypass combined with ring annuloplasty. Clinical and transthoracic echocardiographic follow-up was prospectively performed at discharge and through 60 months.
Technical device success was achieved in all patients. Mitral regurgitation was reduced to none or trace immediately after implantation and remained stable throughout the 5-year follow-up. No device-related major adverse events, structural device failure, implant dislodgement, chordal rupture, reoperation, or rehospitalization occurred. Reverse cardiac remodeling was observed, including reduction in left ventricular end-diastolic diameter and left atrial volume, whereas left ventricular function remained preserved during long-term follow-up.
Surgical implantation of the ChordArt chordal replacement system was simple to perform and demonstrated excellent long-term technical durability and sustained clinical performance over 5 years. These findings support further clinical evaluation of this technology and the ongoing development of a fully transcatheter transseptal delivery platform.

title: Primary, atrial secondary, and ventricular secondary mitral regurgitation in the general population.
authors: Laura Keil; Alexander Hapfelmeier; Jan-Per Wenzel; Julius Nikorowitsch; Daniel Kalbacher; Hermann Reichenspurner; Stefan Blankenberg; Evaldas Girdauskas
journal: Clinical research in cardiology : official journal of the German Cardiac Society
abstract:
While primary mitral valve regurgitation (PMR) results from structural abnormalities of the mitral valve leaflets, secondary mitral valve regurgitation (SMR) arises from either mitral annular dilatation (atrial type, aSMR) or left ventricle remodelling (ventricular type, vSMR) in the absence of intrinsic leaflet disease. Although SMR is considered the most common cause of clinically relevant mitral regurgitation (MR), population-based data on its prevalence, subtype distribution, and clinical profiles are lacking. We aimed to determine the prevalence of PMR and SMR and to characterize PMR, aSMR, and vSMR in the general population.
We analyzed the first 10,000 participants of the population-based Hamburg City Health Study enrolled 2016-2019; 8543 echocardiographic examinations were available. Mitral valve morphology and function were independently assessed by two investigators. PMR was defined by the presence of intrinsic leaflet pathology, whereas SMR was classified as ventricular when left ventricular ejection fraction was less than 50% or less than 55% in the presence of geometric distortion (tenting area ≥ 150 mm2 or coaptation depth ≥ 10 mm) and cases with left ventricular ejection fraction equal to or above 50% were classified as aSMR.
A total of 216 participants had moderate or severe MR (2.53% of the total cohort, 95% confidence interval (CI): 2.20%-2.89%, see Fig. 3). Of these, 148 were classified as SMR (68.5%, 95% CI: 61.8%-74.7%), the remaining were mainly of primary etiology (31.5%, 95% CI: 25.3%-38.2%). Among SMR cases, aSMR was predominant (84.5%, 95% CI: 77.5%-89.9%), whereas vSMR accounted for 15.5% (95% CI: 10.1%-22.4%). Compared with aSMR, individuals with vSMR were older, more symptomatic, and more frequently had atrial fibrillation and hypertension. Echocardiographic parameters indicated more advanced cardiac remodelling and dysfunction in vSMR. Compared with SMR, participants with PMR had greater MR severity, while age and the proportion of women were numerically higher without reaching statistical significance. During a median follow-up of 4.56 years, 10 participants had died, with all-cause mortality being significantly higher among participants with PMR than among those with aSMR.
In this population-based cohort, SMR accounted for two-thirds of relevant MR, with aSMR being the predominant subtype. MR severity was higher in PMR as compared to SMR. Distinct echocardiographic and clinical profiles suggest more advanced disease in vSMR. Multivariate analysis revealed that atrial fibrillation was significantly more present in the vSMR cohort. These findings highlight the need for refined SMR subclassification and longitudinal studies to define prognostic implications and clinically meaningful definitions. All-cause mortality was highest in participants with PMR than in those with aSMR.

title: Documented Valvular Regurgitation and Explicit Heart Failure in an Internal Medicine Registry: A Cross-Sectional Study.
authors: Maria Rada; Maria-Laura Craciun; Ana-Maria Pah; Diana Utu; Dana Emilia Velimirovici; Diana-Maria Mateescu; Ioana Cotet; Ariana Bianca Velciov; Cristiana Adina Avram
abstract: Background and Objectives: Routine records may conflate valvular heart disease (VHD), functional classification, and shared diagnostic assessment. We quantified the cross-sectional association between a registry VHD label and explicitly documented heart failure (HF), while recognizing that every observed valve lesion was regurgitant. Materials and Methods: The analytic sample comprised all 224 eligible adults admitted to the Internal Medicine II Department of a railway-affiliated hospital between 1 August 2025 and 31 July 2026: 38 with documented VHD and 186 without documented VHD. The primary outcome was an explicit HF diagnosis; a combined HF/NYHA-positive field was examined as an over-inclusive sensitivity outcome. Logistic regression was adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, smoking history, and total cholesterol. Results: Explicit HF was documented in 24/38 patients with VHD (63.2%) and 72/186 without VHD (38.7%; adjusted OR 2.87, 95% CI 1.38-5.99). The combined outcome was present in 28/38 (73.7%) and 101/186 (54.3%), respectively (adjusted OR 2.38, 95% CI 1.09-5.21). All 38 exposed patients had documented mitral, aortic, and/or tricuspid regurgitation; no stenosis, prolapse, or prior valve intervention was recorded. Conclusions: Documented valvular regurgitation was associated with explicit HF documentation. Because regurgitation may be secondary to ventricular or atrial disease, reverse causation, shared ascertainment, non-adjudicated diagnoses, and residual confounding preclude causal, temporal, prognostic, or lesion-specific inference.

title: One Pressure, Many Targets: Left Ventricular Filling Pressure as a Candidate Effect Modifier for Non-Invasive Ventilation in Acute Coronary Syndromes.
authors: Marek Tomala
abstract: Non-invasive ventilation relieves acute cardiogenic pulmonary edema and reduces intubation. Whether it saves lives is disputed; restricting the pooled record to the least biased trials leaves neither endpoint significant. My hypothesis: raising pleural pressure subtracts venous return; whether that subtraction is banked as unloading or paid as lost output depends on preload responsiveness, for which left ventricular filling pressure is a candidate effect modifier and not a measure. One radiographic label may contain two gas-exchange phenotypes, proposed for groups, not patients: carbon dioxide accumulates far more slowly than an ischemia-driven presentation floods the alveolus, and the remodeled ventricle arrives hypercapnic. Applied pressure inflates flooded air spaces without removing lung water, lowers left ventricular transmural pressure, and reaches two cardiac submechanisms. The left ventricular arm follows the sign rule; the renal arm follows it only through volume status; and in right ventricular infarction, the recorded filling pressure misleads, while the pulmonary arm does not reverse. In acute coronary syndromes, the first prediction fails if transmural pressure falls no more in the elevated than in the normal stratum, or if stroke volume index does not fall in the latter. The outer boundary is the requirement for emergency reperfusion, a limit inferred rather than measured directly.

title: Initial Clip Selection and Outcomes After Mitral Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair: A Single-Center Experience.
authors: Aysel Akhundova; Berhan Keskin; Umeyir Savur; Özlem Önder; Ebubekir Yiğitbay; Ekrem Guler; Haci Murat Güneş; Mehmet Emir Arman; Bilal Boztosun
abstract: Background: Whether the initial clip type selected during transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) of the mitral valve-grasping width and arm length-independently influences procedural and echocardiographic outcomes remains uncertain. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 138 consecutive patients undergoing mitral TEER. The first implanted clip was classified as narrow standard-length (NT), long narrow-arm (XT), or long wide-arm (XTW). Determinants of initial clip selection and its association with procedural success (residual mitral regurgitation [MR] ≤ 1+), post-procedural transmitral gradient, and the need for ≥2 clips were assessed using multivariable logistic and linear regression. Results: Median age was 74.0 (66.0-80.0), 74.5 (66.0-82.5), and 75.0 (70.0-79.0) years, and median LVEF was 35.0% (30.0-50.0), 30.0% (25.0-45.0), and 40.0% (25.0-45.0), for the NT, XT, and XTW groups, respectively; 66% of patients overall were male. An XTW clip was implanted first in 61.6% of patients. XTW selection was independently associated with larger effective regurgitant orifice area, lower LVEF, longer posterior leaflet length, and secondary MR (all p < 0.05), whereas NT selection favored younger age, smaller orifice, and higher LVEF. After adjustment for these factors, no statistically significant independent association was detected between initial clip type and residual MR ≥2+, post-procedural transmitral gradient, or the need for additional clips (all p > 0.05); however, confidence intervals were wide. On univariable analysis, larger left atrial size and moderate-to-severe tricuspid regurgitation were associated with residual MR ≥ 2+, but neither remained significant after multivariable adjustment. Conclusions: Initial clip selection was associated with valve anatomy, LVEF and MR etiology. No statistically significant independent association between initial clip type and procedural or short-term echocardiographic outcomes was detected in this cohort. Given the observational design, confounding by indication, limited sample size and wide confidence intervals, clinically relevant effects cannot be excluded, and these findings do not establish the superiority or equivalence of any clip-selection strategy.

title: Heart Failure with Recovered Ejection Fraction: EGPA-Associated Cardiomyopathy Treated with Benralizumab.
authors: Laxmi Raj Bangari; Yugant Khand; Vidit Yadav; Aarti Desai; Andrea Muniz; Jose Ruiz; Jose Nativi-Nicolau; Juan Leoni; Parag Patel; Rohan Goswami
abstract: Background: We report a case to demonstrate that targeted eosinophil depletion with Benralizumab (anti-IL-5 receptor α therapy) can induce the complete functional and structural reversal of advanced EGPA-associated cardiomyopathy. Case Presentation: A 56-year-old woman with a decade-long history of EGPA presented with progressive nonischemic dilated cardiomyopathy and a nadir ejection fraction of 25-30%. Cardiac MRI demonstrated diffuse nonischemic late gadolinium enhancement consistent with eosinophil-mediated myocardial injury. Despite the optimization of guideline-directed medical therapy, complete recovery was not achieved until benralizumab was initiated. Following biologic therapy, the ejection fraction recovered to 50% and severe mitral regurgitation regressed to mild. The exercise capacity was preserved throughout, with a peak VO2 of 117% and 111% of predicted before and after biologic therapy, respectively. The patient remains in NYHA Class I at the one-year follow-up. Discussion: We describe a case with EGPA-associated non-ischemic cardiomyopathy treated with benralizumab achieving the complete recovery of ventricular function and achieving the complete independence of steroid therapy. Conclusions: This case emphasizes the importance of identifying the inflammatory etiology of cardiomyopathy, optimizing GDMT systematically, and considering targeted biologic therapy directed at the underlying disease.

title: Coxiella burnetii infective endocarditis involving a valved right ventricle-to-pulmonary artery conduit after Rastelli repair in an adolescent: a case report.
authors: Zonghui Hou; Junxiang Pan; Feiyang Wang; Mengqi Zhao; Xuechen Liu; Lianyi Wang
abstract:
Coxiella burnetii is an important cause of blood culture-negative infective endocarditis (IE). Pediatric C. burnetii endocarditis is rare, particularly in patients with prosthetic cardiovascular materials.
A 13-year-old boy with pulmonary atresia who had undergone Rastelli repair followed by replacement with a valved right ventricle-to-pulmonary artery (RV-PA) conduit presented with recurrent fever and a mobile intraconduit mass. Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) showed a vegetation in the pulmonary valve/conduit region, and cardiac computed tomography (CT) confirmed a corresponding filling defect without periconduit abscess or pseudoaneurysm. Blood metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) detected C. burnetii, while indirect immunofluorescence assay (IFA) showed positive phase I and phase II IgG antibodies. The conduit vegetation and blood detection of C. burnetii fulfilled major imaging and microbiological criteria, respectively, under the 2023 Duke-International Society for Cardiovascular Infectious Diseases criteria. An individualized regimen of doxycycline, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX), and hydroxychloroquine was followed by clinical improvement and reduction in lesion size during hospitalization.
C. burnetii should be considered in children with prosthetic cardiovascular materials who present with persistent fever and negative conventional blood cultures. Molecular testing, serology, and multimodality cardiac imaging can support diagnosis and early follow-up.

title: Apixaban in a Dialysis Patient With Valvular Heart Disease and Calciphylaxis: Rethinking Conventional Anticoagulation.
authors: Miguel Hueso; Aida Valverde-Farré
abstract:
Vitamin K antagonists (VKAs) remain the standard anticoagulation for mechanical heart valves but may promote vascular calcification and calciphylaxis.
An 88-year-old woman with a longstanding mechanical aortic valve and advanced chronic kidney disease developed biopsy-confirmed calciphylaxis during VKA therapy. Following initiation of hemodialysis, anticoagulation was switched to low-dose apixaban (2.5 mg twice a day) with plasma level monitoring. Over 2.5 years of follow-up, no bleeding, thromboembolic events, or valve-related complications occurred, and renal recovery allowed dialysis withdrawal. WHY BEYOND THE GUIDELINES?: Direct oral anticoagulants are contraindicated in patients with mechanical heart valves and not recommended in dialysis. Apixaban was introduced because of VKA-associated calciphylaxis and limited therapeutic alternatives.
Apixaban may be used safely in patients with long-standing mechanical aortic valves because of its predictable pharmacokinetics.
Apixaban may represent a pragmatic option in selected patients with long-standing mechanical aortic valves when guideline-recommended VKA therapy cannot be maintained.

title: Genetic differences between fibroelastic deficiency and Barlow's disease in mitral valve prolapse.
authors: Nina Feirer; Melanie Weber; Stefanie A Doppler; Katharina Knoll; Ling Li; Lucas Miranda; Mengyao Yu; Harald Lahm; Ehsan Vafadarnejad; Muamer Kameric; Tatjana Luzius; Sabine Seeler; Irina Gottmann; Felix Wirth; Marius Schwab; Arnar Geirsson; Peter Lichtner; Aeron M Small; Klaus Berger; Monika Stoll; Rüdiger Lange; Peter Gruber; Heribert Schunkert; Albert Hagége; Nabila Bouatia-Naji; Bertram Müller-Myhsok; Teresa Trenkwalder; Markus Krane; Martina Dreßen
abstract:
Fibroelastic deficiency (FED) and Barlow's disease represent subtypes of degenerative mitral valve prolapse (MVP). Whether these two conditions represent opposite ends of an anatomic spectrum or rather distinct etiologies remains unclear.
To study this question from a genetic perspective, we conducted the first genome-wide association study (GWAS) on anatomical subtypes of MVP, exploring the MVP-Munich and MVP-France cohorts, including 1,064 FED and 821 Barlow's disease cases, and 11,923 controls. Patients were stratified via echocardiographic and surgical reports. GWAS meta-analysis was performed separately for FED and Barlow's disease. The identified risk loci were analyzed via gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), targeted variant-phenotype association analysis, and mitral valve tissue was analyzed in single-nucleus RNA-sequencing.For FED, one risk locus achieved genome-wide significance (p<5e-8) at 5q23.3 (CHSY3). For Barlow's disease, two independent loci with genome-wide significance were identified at 5q35.2 (CPLX2) and 10q26.12 (WDR11). Further 30 additional independent signals showed a suggestive association (p<5e-5) with FED, and 30 different independent signals with Barlow's disease. Targeted variant-phenotype association analysis revealed an association of FED with atrial arrhythmias, while Barlow's disease was associated with atrial and ventricular arrhythmias. In combination with GSEA, our results linked Barlow's disease to changes in cell cycle, transcription, senescence, and ubiquitination. FED was connected to cardiac, valvular, mesoderm, and endoderm development.
This study suggests genetic heterogeneity between FED and Barlow's disease and identifies risk loci for future investigation.

title: Novel cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging biomarkers to track response to treatment including Sotatercept in a patient with idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension: a case report.
authors: Alessandro Castiglione; Barbro Kjellström; Göran Rådegran; Ellen Ostenfeld
abstract:
Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) causes progressive right ventricular (RV) pressure overload and left ventricular (LV) underfilling. Sotatercept is an activin-signal inhibitor, approved by FDA in 2024 and EMA in 2025, as an add-on treatment in adult patients with PAH. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR)-derived atrioventricular plane displacement (AVPD) and left ventricular pressure-volume (PV) loops may represent non-invasive markers of treatment response, particularly important as novel therapies addressing remodelling emerge.
A 30-year-old woman was diagnosed with idiopathic PAH, after presenting with dyspnoea and peripheral oedema. Baseline CMR showed severe RV dilation, reduced RV ejection fraction, and low indexed LV stroke volume, with reduced bilateral AVPD and markedly impaired LV PV loop indices, with low stroke work, low mean external power, and high ventriculo-arterial coupling. Initial dual PAH therapy, with an endothelin receptor antagonist and a phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitor initially improved symptoms, pulmonary vascular resistance, as well as AVPD and PV loop derived indices, whereas conventional CMR indices showed only minimal change. One year later, despite triple therapy, including prostacyclin analogue, the patient deteriorated clinically and CMR showed worsening of AVPD and PV loop indices. Treatment escalation with Sotatercept immediately improved clinical status, haemodynamic, AVPD, and PV loop indices despite persistent RV remodelling.
Serial CMR-derived AVPD and LV PV loops may provide clinically useful additional information during longitudinal follow-up of PAH patients, especially in those approaching maximal available medical therapies. In the present case, both AVPD and LV PV loops reflected treatment response, and showed significant improvement after initiation of Sotatercept.
